First listed 2026-01-05 · episode or wrap

2026 Predictions with Dan Ives and Chris Verrone | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 40

The panel favors continued AI investment and broader market participation while debating power constraints, model economics, interest rates and valuation. Ives emphasizes enterprise adoption and specific AI beneficiaries; Verrone prefers bank leadership, contrarian sectors and price trends; Eisman tests financing, housing supply and conditional AI risks. Primary records support Apple’s Gemini catalyst and Eisman’s resistance to rapid Fed-cut expectations. Some bullish supporting premises are overstated, including enterprise adoption, Oracle backlog timing and Palantir’s sales model. Full-year targets remain open, and first-half rotation lacks matched return verification.

YouTube · 2026-01-05 ↗Substack · 2026-01-05 ↗Substack · 2026-01-05 ↗
Substantive outcomes and reasoning are separated from supporting numeric mistakes. Eisman asks informative falsification questions and explicitly withholds a Tesla investment, but broad enthusiasm does not define a measurable portfolio return. Full-year and multiyear forecasts retain open horizons; elapsed first-half calls remain unresolved where primary return data are missing.

How he reasons here

  • Keep structural technology adoption separate from equity valuation and drawdowns.
  • Use bank participation and credit spreads as cross-market checks, while specifying signal rules before backtesting.
  • Challenge demand forecasts through power availability, monetization and funding.
  • Separate a conditional downside mechanism from a prediction that it will occur.
  • Use multi-year cash-flow scenarios without assuming every expensive stock will become a historical winner.
